sentence_stem: Because there were many sheep in the field,
correct_completion: the farmer needed two dogs to help him.
full_sentence: Because there were many sheep in the field, the farmer needed two dogs to help him.
acceptable_variants: the farmer asked his son to help him.
the farmer hired a new worker.

options.text: so the farmer had no sheep at all.
options.why_wrong: The stem says there were many sheep, so this completion contradicts the situation it describes.

options.text: the farmer needed two dogs to help him.
we saw the geese swimming in the lake.
options.why_wrong: This describes different animals and a different place, so it does not complete the cause-and-effect logic of 'because'.

options.text: the sun was shining very brightly.
options.why_wrong: This describes the weather, but it does not show a result of the large number of sheep in the field.

explanation: 'Because' introduces a reason, so the second clause must describe the result of the situation in the first clause. The large number of sheep is the reason the farmer needs help. Learners may find 'sheep' confusing because its singular and plural forms are the same, so check the verb form that follows.
translation: Оскільки на полі було багато овець, фермеру потрібні були дві собаки, щоб допомогти йому.
